_doc: Hand-written narrative inputs of the third-pass report, completed in the fourth session of 2026-11-15 (write_test_status.py formats the counts in; make_doc.py writes REPORT.md). The run results below were copied from what was seen.
result_paragraph: Gate Q16 is **not passing** and `passes` is set nowhere. By decision DD-PM-01 there are still **0 documented camera positions** (a coordinate, a lens and a plate): none of the {n_statements} position statements (Library of Congress records, National Park Service reports, place pages and the Record of Treatment) is one. What is new: (1) the National Park Service names the camera place of two catalogued exposures as a building of known outline, the first documented camera places: the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge (view north: records 2018671576 and 2014646001, poses P27 north and P28 northwest, two words of two NPS texts for one exposure) and the gatehouse (view east: record 2012647704, pose P29); their height, lens and exact heading are not documented. (2) The pass criteria of the tests at those places were written before the renders (criteria.json). Results: P27 {v27}, P28 {v28}, P29 {v29}; P13 (rendered now) {v13}. The three binary tests of the first criterion are necessary conditions only (the superseded poses P06 and P07 pass them too and are does not); the skyline tests fit the heading, the lens and a vertical shift to the photograph and are compared with 24 control stations: {sky27}; {sky28}; {sky29}. No pose is called a match. (3) The Record of Treatment prints {n_figs} captioned 1863 photographs with a direction of view; {n_tied_all} are tied to catalogued Library of Congress records ({n_ties} by image match confirmed by looking, {n_plate} of them with same-plate geometry; the others by the Digital ID in the caption), the others are prints of the park and other collections. The image ties of the six Metropolitan Museum items show that the first run's P04 and P05 are the two plates of one Library panorama (record 2014646002). (4) A wider search of the Library of Congress (the whole Civil War group) added {n_wide} records ({n_wide_tied} tied to a catalogued exposure by looking; {n_rej} high-scoring matches were rejected on looking): the registry now holds {n_records} records and {n_poses} poses. (5) Re-running the renderer reproduced the renders of the earlier sessions pixel for pixel (see the determinism line below). (6) The fourth session (2026-11-15) finished what the restarts of 2026-11-14 had cut short: P29 rendered and its sheet looked at, the verdicts of P13, P27, P28 and P29 written (the P29 verdict is weak: the skyline test does not tell the gatehouse from its neighbours), a full re-run of all 20 poses reproduced every render byte for byte, an error in the drafted P29 text found and fixed (18 of the 24 control stations fit better than the gatehouse, not 6), and the registry texts that said no place or direction was stated where the Park Service gives one corrected. What would settle Q16: station coordinates, lens and plate from the park (an owner step), the height and 1863 form of the gatehouse, a 1863 near-field model, landmark coordinates good to a few metres, and a value for T-Q16-1 written before the match (all in PHOTOMATCH.md).
what_was_run: State found: the earlier run of this pass was cut short by the container restart at 00:05 UTC (renders of P27 and P28 never made, the wide-search script run only in part, a P13 sheet without a verdict). Continued from it, nothing redone: every saved image file was re-hashed (436 files match their ledger entries; 11 entries are working copies or originals that were deleted by design), the wide search was completed and the poses rendered.

`wide_search.py` (completed; the not-digitized records are now recorded as such, not as failures): 183 photographs of 1863 naming Gettysburg in the open JSON search of the whole Civil War group (950 results), {n_wide} not held before; 57 medium JPEGs saved at 1 request per second (one truncated download re-fetched), 5 records not digitized; the 62 item records fetched; each image looked at on four contact sheets and classified by hand (`wide_data.py`): staged flags set on 6 (the sharpshooter and Devil's Den series, the posed scene of 11 November, a print whose printed number 251 is the sharpshooter negative).

`scan_nps_photos.py`: one fixed rule over all 118 saved NPS texts and pages: 340 passages that give a place or direction of view of a photograph, 15 already statements; read in full. It found the Record of Treatment figure captions (about forty 1863 photographs with a direction and a park number) that no earlier pass had used, and confirmed that no NPS publication or page read gives a coordinate, a lens or a plate.

`nps_figures.py`: the two PDFs of the Record of Treatment (294 and 189 MB) fetched again with one request each (sha256 equal to the manifest of the first fetch), 36 captions cut verbatim from the saved text and the 36 images extracted with pdfimages (the historic photographs are stored inverted: inverted to positive), the PDFs deleted; {n_fig_stmts} new figure statements generated (5 of the 36 captions were already statements).

`match_third_pass.py` (SIFT, ratio test, RANSAC; one FLANN index per candidate; through the machine lock, about 25 minutes): 36 figure images, {n_wide} wide-search images and the 6 Metropolitan Museum items against 288 catalogued images; {n_ties} figure ties confirmed by looking at both images (nps_figures_confirmed.json) in addition to the ties by Digital ID; {n_wide_tied} wide records tied to a catalogued exposure after looking at the pairs side by side on eight sheets; {n_rej} high-scoring matches rejected on looking (studio portraits and a flag card matched to landscapes by texture alone); all six Metropolitan Museum items are catalogued Library photographs (met_ties_confirmed.json).

`tie_geometry.py` (thresholds fixed before it was run; about 25 seconds of CPU, run directly with nice because it is under the 30-second limit): the homography of every accepted tie is described by inlier fraction, scale, rotation, anisotropy, perspective, residual and footprint. Of the {n_ties} confirmed figure ties {n_plate} are same plate (inlier fraction {plate_frac_min} to {plate_frac_max}, median residual {plate_res_min} to {plate_res_max} px) and {n_not_plate} are same scene by the rule (a print turned 4.2 degrees against the 4.0-degree bar; a small detail with few features): both were called the same photograph by looking and say so in their notes. The two Metropolitan plates of P04 and P05 cover 0.00 to 0.53 and 0.45 to 0.96 of the width of the Library panorama 2014646002 (met_ties_confirmed.json).

Poses and criteria: P13 rendered and looked at; P27 and P28 (one exposure, two NPS words) and P29 (the view east, which the matching showed to be record 2012647704) registered with their pre-written criteria (criteria.json: C-P27-P28-1 at 00:01:29Z by the interrupted run, C-P27-P28-2 at 00:31:42Z, C-P29-1 at 00:44:11Z, each before the render or the model skyline of its pose); the renders made through the lock; `measure_c1.py` (the three binary tests; the definition was written before the render and tested only on the other poses P06 and P07); `skyline_test.py` (24 control stations each; the first computation of the model skyline was a smoke test on the station only, run after the criteria were written; the lock run reproduces it).

Statements: {n_statements} (was 70): the Record of Treatment figures, the record texts of the wide search (leads where the Library cites Frassanito), the caption of the Culp's Hill print; evidence lines R12.032 to R12.035 rebuilt (every quote checked again against the saved text: 0 failures); the library pointers (acquired_3.json, status_3.json) updated; five blocked or failed sources recorded (NARA catalog, five records not digitized, the Sketch Book text, a Gutenberg edition that does not exist, the lodge-roof negative now found).

Document and registry rebuilt from the data (`catalogue_wide_items.py`, `build_registry.py`, `make_doc.py`); `add_verdicts_third_pass.py` wrote the verdicts of P13, P27, P28 and P29 after the sheets and the lines-on-photograph images were looked at.

Fourth session, 2026-11-15 (the machine had been restarted again; nothing finished was redone). State found: P29 registered but never rendered; verdicts.json still at the second-pass state (16 pose verdicts); the P29 verdict text written but guarded by an assert that waits for its sheet note; the Q16 test file red (8 of 15 passing); PHOTOMATCH.md and REPORT.md of the second pass.

`run.mjs P29` through the machine lock (slot granted at once; 3 renders in 7 s), then a full re-run of all 20 poses (120 PNG, 32 s) into tmp/photomatch/renders_rerun with PM_RENDER_DIR: every file is byte-identical to the one in tmp/photomatch/renders (P13, P27 and P28 were made on 2026-11-13 and 14; P29 a few seconds earlier in the same job), and the 96 files of the second pass kept in renders_prev.sha256 are still identical (96 of 96). `record_determinism.py` wrote render_determinism.json (a sha256 per file); the test file checks it. Software GL on this machine class only.

`compose.py P29` and `overlay_lines.py P29`; all 20 pose sheets (P01 to P29) and the lines images of P27, P28 and P29 were opened and looked at in this session and every verdict was read against its sheet: none needed to change (the renders are byte-identical to those the earlier passes looked at). `measure_p29_sheet.py` reads descriptive numbers from the frozen skyline rule of C-P29-1 and the three P29 renders (not a criterion).

Error found and fixed in the drafted P29 verdict text: it counted the control stations that fit better as 25 minus the rank (6), but skyline_test.py ranks from the best fit, so rank 19 means 18 of the 24 controls fit better (checked against the stored controls: 18 below, 6 above); the text now says 18 and a test pins it. The draft's sentence about the size of the 1863 canopy of Culp's Hill (17 m at 1 km) had no source for a canopy height and was rewritten as arithmetic with the assumption named. `add_verdicts_third_pass.py` was run once.

Registry refresh (`registry_data.py`, `build_registry.py`): five texts that said no place or direction is stated where the Record of Treatment gives one were rewritten (2018670660 said 'no place is stated beyond near the centre of the battlefield' while Figures 6 and 29 call it a view southwest from the Rose Barn; 2012647719, 2012647700, 91732551, 2018672207), 2018670660 is now classed near field (a grave trench with grave boards and a wagon: nothing of the model in the frame) instead of camera place not fixed, and every unposed record that the Record of Treatment concerns now quotes its statement from the statement file (13 records).

Reproduction of the numbers behind the verdicts, run directly with nice because each took under 10 s of CPU (the 30-second rule): `measure_c1.py` (its sha256 is the one recorded in criteria.json when the criterion was written; the 12 stored measurements are reproduced exactly from the current renders), `skyline_test.py P29` (5.6 s of CPU) and `skyline_test.py P28` (7.3 s; the P27 and P28 sector case): both cases reproduce the stored results exactly, controls included. A cross-check of the two implementations of the same pose in `measure_p29_sheet.py`: the silhouette of the WebGL render and the ray-marched skyline of skyline_test.py at the same station, height, heading and field differ by 0.33 degrees RMS (7.7 px of 570, at most 15 px; the render lies a mean 5.8 px lower): the render and the test see the same camera, and the difference is far smaller than the 0.31 of the frame height (about 170 px) between the render and the photograph.

Source re-checks of this session: every quote of the 145 statements was searched again in the saved text of its source (143 found after whitespace normalisation, 141 of them as exact strings; the 2 not found, PS-NPS-SPEN-7 and PS-NPS-SPEN-8, are the statements marked read from the page image because the text layer is garbled: the two pages (58 and 59 of the Slaughter Pen report) were rendered and read again and carry the quoted words); every saved image file was re-hashed against both ledgers (436 and 57 files verified, 0 mismatches; 11 first-run entries have their originals deleted by design; 20 first-run entries are large derivatives that the records do not offer, the medium file being kept; 5 wide-search records are not digitized by the Library); the archive.org OCR text of Gardner's Sketch Book (volumes I and II, 33 KB and 29 KB, fetched again with two requests, sha256 4bca1403... and 54bdfb62...) is again unusable: it reads the binding decoration, not the letterpress (99 words of five letters or more in volume I, none of them from a plate), so the plate captions remain readable only from the page images (the JP2 zips are 150 MB each).

`check_governance.py` was run once (0.2 s): exit 0, 0 of 969 sub-requirements passing, its coverage lines for Q17, Q18 and Q23 fail on other workstreams' unfinished work (output in tmp/photomatch/work/check_governance_20261115.out).

Negative search for a coordinate in the pictures themselves: the 47 JPEG files saved from the National Park Service Then-And-Now pages (the Library 'then' pictures and the park's modern 'now' pictures, tmp/library/web/photomatch/www.nps.gov) were read for EXIF: 25 carry an EXIF block (Canon EOS 60D or 80D, taken 2016 to 2018, focal lengths 18 to 35 mm of the modern lens), 0 carry a GPS block. No coordinate there; the modern focal length is not the lens of the 1863 exposure and is not used.

`wide_extra_images.py` (new): the first catalogue run had saved every resource that its records offer (228 of 228, checked again), the wide search only the first resource of each of its 62 records. The 51 further resources of 43 wide-search records (second stereo halves, card backs and mount versos, copy negatives) were fetched at 1 request per second (sizes equal to what the records declare, every file decoded) and 31 card backs were fetched again at 1024 px (`--ledger-large`) to read their print; all in wide_extra_images_ledger.json (82 entries). All 94 images of the 8 contact sheets were looked at and the printed captions of 15 card backs read at 1024 px (War Photograph and Exhibition Company Nos. 243, 245, 253, 259, 266, 274, 2288, 2391, 2401; Tipton Nos. 514 to 516; Anthony labels; Mumper and series lists): they describe what a picture shows (in the wheat-field; trees near Culp's Hill; where one gun stood), none states a camera place or a direction. A sentence per record (43) was added to the registry (`wide_extra_data.py`, `build_registry.py`), and a test pins the ledger.
findings: The National Park Service's Record of Treatment (2018) is a source of camera directions and, for some, camera places for about forty July 1863 photographs (park numbers 2B-2063, 2B-2090 and so on); the park's own catalogue is the next step toward stations (owner step). The captions double as 1863 landscape evidence (orchards, fences, woodlots of the Rose, Sherfy, Weikert and McPherson farms): the nps-landscape and vegetation lanes may cite them.
The model's outline of the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse is the 2023 footprint with the right-hand addition; the camera stood on or in the 1855 building (EG-13).
Two NPS texts give two words for the direction of the lodge-roof view, north and northwest; read from the photograph (an exploratory reading, not a test) the heading lies at their boundary (EG-14).

The Leister house photograph (cwpb 00887) is called a view north along the Taneytown Road by the Then-And-Now page and a view northwest by the Record of Treatment: a 45-degree conflict carried as statements; pose P18 follows the first.

The old test tests/photomatch.test.mjs fails on the new ledger and schema (request note bt-web-photomatch-old-test.md); the Q16 section of GATE-SPEC should be refreshed from the files (request note bt-gates-photomatch-third-pass.md).

A feature-match score is not an identification: six matches of 109 to 286 inliers were false (studio portraits and a card with a flag matched to landscapes, a road view matched to a stereo card), and the rule class of tie_geometry.py disagreed with the eye for two true ties (reported as the rule gave them). Every tie was therefore looked at, and the stereo cards were called by looking at their halves.

The first run's poses P04 and P05 (Metropolitan Museum prints) are the two plates of the Library panorama 2014646002 (View of Gettysburg from the Northwest); the Seminary Ridge standpoint of both is still an assumption and the verdict (does not) is on that assumed pose.

The Record of Treatment and the other National Park Service texts disagree on the direction of two Library photographs without a place: park print 2B-2083a (record 2018672207, Little Round Top slope) is a view southeast in the Record of Treatment, against southwest near Devil's Den and northwest at Wheatfield Road and Crawford Avenue in the vista report; park print 2B2086 (record 2018670709) is a view south there. Carried as statements, none chosen.

The camera place of the Library record 2018670660 (five images of one exposure) is the Rose Barn according to the Record of Treatment (view southwest), but the frame holds only a grave trench, grave boards, a tree and a wagon train: a near-field view that the bare-earth model cannot be compared with; the barn is a point of the model (error 10 m), not a footprint.

A fitted skyline cannot decide a station: for P29 the three best-fitting of 24 control stations lie 200 to 300 m east or south-east on ground 17 to 19 m lower, and the fit is as good at 5 m, 8 m and 11 m camera height (0.53 to 0.58 degrees).

The verso of the Tyson card 2019635468 ([Gettysburg from Seminary Ridge]) carries, besides the studio stamp and the ink word Gettysburg (all the Library transcribes), a faint pencil note in another hand: 'original by Tyson in August 1863' (read at 1024 px; hand and date of the note unknown). If it is right the view is of August, not of July 1863; the record stays inside the July terrain scope as a lead, flagged in its registry entry.

The second resource of record 2014647511 (John Burns, the hero of Gettysburg / Slaughter pen at Gettysburg) is the verso of the card, a second picture: a small print of the slaughter pen with the card's caption No. 253. The registry had said the verso was not shown; it now says what it shows (a near-field wood view).
tests: `node --test docs/battle-theatre/app/tests/photomatch-q16.test.mjs` (run directly: no browser, 12 s): 23 tests, 22 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the optional render test). At the start of this session the file had 16 tests: 10 pass, 5 fail, 1 skipped (the data had run ahead of its checks: no verdicts yet for P13, P27, P28 and P29, P29 not rendered). Seven tests were added this session: the packer's own copy-audit rules on PHOTOMATCH.md (the document had carried tool paths and one working-process word, now removed; the rebuild commands moved into this report); the ledger of the further resources; review sheets present; the skyline wording of the verdict texts against the stored controls (the P29 text must say 18 of the 24 controls fit better); the P29 sheet numbers; the render determinism record; the staged-flag rule. The thresholds of tie_geometry.py and the pre-written criteria are asserted unchanged; no test was loosened.

`node --test tests/photomatch.test.mjs` (the old test in the repository's tests/ folder, outside this task's ownership): 6 tests, 2 pass, 3 fail, 1 skipped: it asserts archive.org-only ledger urls, gazetteer-only pose anchors and the first-run verdicts.json shape; unchanged since the second pass (request notes bt-web-photomatch-old-test.md and bt-gates-photomatch-test-host-rule.md). It is not part of the app suite.

`PHOTOMATCH_RENDER=1 tools/horde/bench.sh node --test docs/battle-theatre/app/tests/photomatch-q16.test.mjs` and `tools/horde/bench.sh node --test docs/battle-theatre/app/tests/*.test.mjs` (the full app suite, 40 files): queued behind the machine lock at 23:05 and 23:09 UTC; result below if it came before this report was written.
owed: No real-GPU rendering: every render is software GL (SwiftShader); nothing here is a timing or a real-GPU visual result.
No master TIFF beyond the two Cemetery Hill views (4096-px working copies kept); no full-resolution matching.

The NARA catalog (reachable, but a JavaScript shell only: its API needs a key, an owner act), the 5 records of the wide search that the Library has not digitized, the Sketch Book letterpress (images only at 1024 px) and the NARA Prologue blog on the Devil's Den sharpshooter (the PDF's source for the staged flag; a host that was not in the list of reachable hosts) were not read.
Figures of the Record of Treatment that no catalogued image matched are statements without a photograph; the park's catalogue numbers (GETT 41135) need the park's help (owner step).
The skyline test could not be applied to the other poses: they have no documented place, and the NPS area words (a farm, a hill) do not fix the camera within the depth of the scene.

Delegated decisions DD-PM-06 to DD-PM-10 were appended to decisions/DELEGATED-DECISIONS-2026-11-11.md on 2026-11-14 (the section 'Added 2026-11-14 by bt-web photo-match'); DD-G16 of bt-gates takes the same reading of the plan's wording. The fourth session appended two delegated decisions to the same file (DD-PM-11: the further resources of the wide-search records are fetched and looked at like those of the first catalogue; DD-PM-12: a pencil date note on a verso keeps its record in the July scope as a flagged lead); the corrections it made (a counted rank, five registry texts, one registry class) are corrections of what the sources and the files say, not choices among alternatives.
